top_stories.title: Big Tech rally: Mag 7 comeback powered by cloud earnings
points: The Magnificent 7 (Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta) jumped 4%+ Monday via the Roundhill MAGS ETF, its best day since March, after being nearly flat for seven months.
S&P 500 rose 1.5% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1.3% to a record high; six of seven mega-caps rose 3%+ while Apple fell ~1.8%.
Microsoft +4.9%, Amazon +4.6%, Alphabet +4.4%, Meta +6.1%, Oracle +9.6% on the session.
Microsoft Azure grew 43% to a $100B annual run rate, Amazon Web Services grew 37% to $42.2B, and Google Cloud surged 82% to $24.8B.
The three cloud giants added nearly $1.5 trillion in combined market value in a week; hyperscaler (large-scale AI data center operator) capex is projected up 70% this year to over $700 billion.
Mag 7 valuations had compressed to their cheapest level versus the market in years, setting up a 'catch-up trade'.

unique_angles.point: Cites a $2.3 trillion compute-demand backlog across the top four cloud providers and Iran conflict de-escalation as rally drivers; Goldman Sachs frames multiple compression as a major break from the dot-com era.
Nvidia reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company at a $5 trillion valuation.
S&P 500 futures up 0.1% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.7% premarket as focus shifts to earnings.
Alphabet posted its first-ever quarter of negative free cash flow, which investors shrugged off.

top_stories.title: Free cash flow becomes the key Big Tech metric as AI debt looms
points: Heavy data center spending has eroded the cash-generation profile that made Big Tech a safe haven; Alphabet and others are now showing negative free cash flow (cash left after capital expenditures).
Citadel Securities (Ken Griffin's firm) forecasts a $500 billion wave of new Big Tech borrowing for data center chips.
Analysts call the potential scale 'unprecedented,' possibly forming one of the largest new investment-grade credit segments (debt rated as high quality by ratings agencies).
Price-to-earnings multiples are compressing across mega-cap tech despite revenue growth, as investors broaden bets beyond the top five names.

unique_angles.point: Frames the market's shift from treating huge capex as a red flag to treating it as a growth catalyst.

Shares fell 12% Monday to their lowest level since August 2024.
Investor Michael Burry exited his GameStop position entirely.
CEO Ryan Cohen's credibility took a hit after a failed August attempt to acquire eBay.

top_stories.title: AMD earnings in focus for AI momentum
points: AMD reports today with investors looking for evidence it is extending its artificial intelligence momentum.
AMD shares have more than doubled this year.
Traders are pricing in a sizable post-earnings move as Wall Street debates whether chip stocks are set to recover from recent weakness.

items.title: Missouri votes on eliminating its income tax
points: Amendment 5 would phase down Missouri's individual income tax rate with full elimination targeted for 2032.
Individual income taxes bring in over $9 billion a year, 63% of state general revenue in FY2025.
Lawmakers would get authority to expand and raise other levies, including the 4.225% state sales tax, to offset the loss.
Supporters cite competitiveness for business investment; opponents warn of cost-of-living hits and cuts to education, law enforcement, healthcare, and infrastructure.
Nine states have no income tax today: Florida, Nevada, South Dakota, Texas, Washington, Wyoming, Alaska (1980), Tennessee (2021), New Hampshire (2025).
Wisconsin created the first modern state income tax in 1911; most states adopted them after the Great Depression and again after WWII.

issues.subject: Is This The Next State To Eliminate Income Tax?

headlines: Missouri voters decide today on Amendment 5 to eliminate income tax by 2032, requiring lawmakers to offset $9B annual revenue through higher sales taxes and other levies.
SpaceX releases first quarterly results as a public company, with investors focused on Starlink growth and capital spending guidance.
Marijuana use has surpassed cigarette smoking in the U.S., marking a significant shift in consumption patterns.
FAA certifies Boeing 737 Max 7 after nearly a decade-long regulatory review, clearing another aircraft variant for commercial operation.
Trump administration criticized for calling out Exxon and Chevron for 'making too much money,' signaling potential policy pressure on energy sector profitability.

sections.title: Missouri's Historic Income Tax Decision
points: Amendment 5 would gradually reduce Missouri's individual income tax rate with complete elimination targeted for 2032.
Individual income taxes currently generate over $9 billion annually and comprise 63% of the state's general revenue in FY2025.
To compensate for lost revenue, lawmakers would gain authority to expand and raise other levies, including sales tax which currently stands at 4.225%.

Supporters argue the measure makes Missouri more competitive for investment and business growth, while opponents worry about cost-of-living impacts and potential cuts to education, law enforcement, healthcare, and infrastructure funding.

sections.title: State Income Tax Landscape
points: Nine U.S. states currently have no income tax: Florida, Nevada, South Dakota, Texas, Washington, Wyoming, Alaska (eliminated 1980), Tennessee (eliminated 2021), and New Hampshire (eliminated 2025).
Historically, states relied on property taxes and poll taxes until Wisconsin implemented the first modern individual income tax in 1911.
Most states adopted income taxes after the Great Depression due to collapsing property values, with another wave following World War II.

sections.title: Magnificent 7 Valuation Reset Sparks Comeback

Google Cloud achieved 82% growth to $24.8B—the strongest of the three—allowing investors to overlook Alphabet's first-ever quarter of negative free cash flow (cash generated after capital expenditures), indicating heavy reinvestment.
